reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that profit arises not from change per se but from the mismatch between anticipated and realized outcomes due to imperfect foresight. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian updating where prior beliefs about future prices (P) diverge from posterior estimates after observing new data. This divergence creates exploitable arbitrage opportunities. In GSE, the same principle underpins state transitions: when agents update beliefs based on changing conditions, the system shifts from one equilibrium to another—this shift is profit. The mathematical duality lies in treating uncertainty as both a constraint (in GSI) and a dynamic variable (in GSE). Failure modes include overconfidence in prediction models (leading to zero profit), or misalignment between agent expectations and environmental dynamics (causing systemic inefficiency).
